output:
Dear all,

I’ve just come off nights and caught up with the thread. First, I’m genuinely thrilled that Amma and Appa want to come. Having them here for ordinary days with the children, rather than trying to fit everything into a short visit, means so much to me. Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable, including “Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays”. Amma, I’m afraid your diary is filling up.

Kiran, you’re right that I should have spoken to you earlier, before the paperwork was under way. I started it because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, and that was exactly when I should have looped you in. I’m sorry. You should have had a chance to talk this through with us, not heard about it once it sounded settled.

The idea first came up on the phone in August, when Rohan showed Appa the vegetable patch and Appa said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” That got us talking about a longer stay. It’s a lovely prospect, but my excitement isn’t a reason to skip the practical questions you’ve raised.

On Appa’s heart, I agree we need a proper plan. Dr. Prakash has agreed to review him in March before they fly, and to do a video consultation in July. He’s also happy to share his notes with me, with Appa’s agreement, so we can keep the information together. The March review needs to guide us on whether the journey and length of stay are sensible.

I’ve got a travel insurance quote of about £640 each for the six months, including pre-existing cardiac cover. The agent says Appa’s stent is covered, but I want that confirmed in the policy wording, along with exclusions, limits and what happens if he needs treatment or has to come home. It’s a quote at this stage, not cover already in place, and we shouldn’t assume NHS treatment would be free. Leicester Royal is fifteen minutes away and I know many of the cardiology team, which is reassuring, but that isn’t a substitute for insurance or continuity with Dr. Prakash.

The annexe is finished: it’s on the ground floor, with no steps and its own shower with a grab rail. They’ll have their own space, not just our spare room.

You’re right about six months being a big change for Amma, too. The proposed dates are the first week of April to the end of September 2027. The long-term visitor visa allows a maximum of six months per visit; it doesn’t mean they have to stay that long. The return ticket will be flexible. Amma, if six weeks turns out to be enough, or you miss home sooner, we can change things. There’s no obligation to stay until September for our sake.

And Pune for Ganesh Chaturthi needn’t be lost. They could fly from here to Pune in September and finish the trip there. Or, if it suits you all, the Pune family could come here in August—I’d be very happy to cover your flights. Those are possibilities to talk about, not decisions made for anyone.

Could we all have a video call this Sunday at 4pm UK / 9.30pm India? I’d like us to hear what Amma and Appa want, talk through the worries properly, and leave room to change the plan.

Love,
Meera
